newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen firm after Q4 GDP.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen firm after Q4 GDP.

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to rise after a report on the fourth-quarter gross domestic product, analysts said.
-- PHIL ORLANDO, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER OF VALUE LINE'S ASSET MANAGEMENT DIVISION

--- The deflator is good, the nominal GDP number is bad ... near the high end of expectations. But we were hoping for a deflator in the two-percent neighborhood. One-point-four percent is materially better than expected on the inflation front and that is the more important number to focus on.

-- "We knew the fourth quarter would have an aberrantly strong GDP, but our near-term concern was the trend in inflation which this report suggests was even more benign than we believed. I think bonds will rally once traders figure this out."

The Commerce Department reported gross domestic product grew at a rate of 4.7 percent in the fourth quarter after an increase of 2.1 percent in the final estimate of the third quarter. The implicit price deflator rose 1.4 percent compared to a 1.7 percent rise in the third quarter.
U.S. economists in a Reuters poll expected the fourth quarter GDP to rise by 3.9 percent.
-- PETER CARDILLO, DIRECTOR OF RESEARCH AT WESTFALIA INVESTMENTS:

-- "The deflator was really good, and that is giving strength to the bond market and should give (stocks) a pop to the upside. But as we approach the higher end of the trading range caution should be used in the big cap stocks that have been running high."
-- LARRY WACHTEL, ANALYST AT PRUDENTIAL SECURITIES:
-- "The inflation element was quite encouraging...If bonds hold up this way stocks will follow up."
The 30-year Treasury bond was up 4/32 to yield 6.86 percent in trading after the release of the data.
